metadata.name: Act on web pages
metadata.author: recued-core
metadata.description: Use “Act on web pages” in Recued. Do up to 20 steps across tabs in one call: read, type, click, press keys, send forms, scroll, wait, go to an address, go back, reload or close a tab. Steps that only read ask nothing; the others ask you once, unless you've allowed them on that site, listing each step and the text it types, never a password. Answers per tab.

page.help: The page the first step runs on: its address, such as https://example.com/orders, whether a tab shows it or not (a new tab opens for it when none does), or a page handle an earlier answer gave, copied exactly. Leave it empty when the first step names its tab with "page" or "url".
page.label: Page

steps.help: The steps, in order, each an object. A step may name its tab: "page":"<handle>", or "url":"https://…" for the tab showing that address (a new tab opens for it when none does); a step naming neither runs on the tab of the step before, so one call can work on several tabs. Reading: {"do":"read"} answers the page as an outline, {"do":"read","form":"text"} as its text; add "find":"See also" for one section (in the text, also #See_also or a CSS selector) or "from":213 to read on. Asking: {"do":"ask","question":"Who designed it?"} has a separate AI answer from the tab's text, quoting it. Reads and asks of different tabs run side by side, so ask each tab its question in one call. Acting: {"do":"type","ref":"e3","value":"text"} types into a field; add "submit":true to then send its form, and for a field that suggests as you type (a city, a contact, a company) "pick":"London, UK" to choose the suggestion with that text. For a password, a PIN or a sign-in code, never write the secret: {"do":"type","text":"Password","secret":"password"} ("PIN", "sign-in code") types the one saved for that field on that site, or asks for it at that step. {"do":"click","ref":"e7"}. {"do":"press","ref":"e3","key":"Enter"} presses a key in it (Escape, Tab, ArrowDown, Control+Enter). {"do":"submit","ref":"e5"} sends the form an element is in. {"do":"scroll"} goes a screen down ("to":"previous", "top" or "bottom"). {"do":"wait","seconds":2}, {"do":"wait","selector":"#results"} until it shows ("until":"gone" until it goes), or {"do":"wait","url_includes":"/inbox"} until the address holds it. {"do":"go","address":"https://…"} loads an address in the tab; {"do":"back"}, {"do":"reload"} and {"do":"close"} do what they say; {"do":"hover","ref":"e9"} points at a menu that opens under the pointer. {"do":"download","ref":"e12"} saves the file a link leads to among the user's files ("address":"https://…/report.pdf" for a file's own address; a public file is fetched by the server, up to 25 MB, needing no tab), answering its file ref for reading it. {"do":"upload","ref":"e7","file":"file:…"} puts one of the user's files (its file ref, from a download or file.search) into a file field; it always asks the user. Name an element by its ref from the latest read of that page, or by its "text", what it shows or is called there ({"do":"click","text":"Sign in"}, with "role":"button" when several share it), which is found when the step runs, so it works after a step loads a new page, as a "selector" does; a ref read before then is found there the same way, by what it showed. To go through pages, chain them: {"do":"click","text":"Next"},{"do":"read"},{"do":"click","text":"Next"},{"do":"read"} reads two more pages in one call. A step may add "success_when", such as {"url_includes":"/orders/"}, {"shows":".toast"}, {"gone":".spinner"}, {"text":"Saved"} or {"page_changes":true}, and "fail_when", such as {"shows":".error"}, {"text":"Invalid"} or {"url_includes":"/login"}, each with "seconds" up to 10; whichever holds first decides. Without success_when, a sent form must load a page or change the address. An action may add "then_read":"#results", a CSS selector for where its result shows: that part is waited for, then read into the answer, so nothing needs reading after. It also stops at a CAPTCHA, or an error message a click or a sent form leads to. At most 20 steps and 30 seconds of waiting.
steps.label: Steps
